memory_candidates.content: When a dispatch file carries a 'Batch Gate Deferral' directive, a plan phase's own verification criterion can literally say 'run the complete unnarrowed gate set' (Verification Tier: full) while the dispatch directive requires discharging it against a scoped narrowing invocation (verify-deploy.sh --skip-slow --only-gate N[,M...], chosen to cover the files that phase actually touched) instead. The dispatch directive takes precedence over the plan's literal task text for that one phase; the full gate still runs once at the batch level and its result attributes back via modified_files. Attempting the unnarrowed full gate set directly in a single-task dispatch risked a 580s timeout with no captured output.

A plan phase's forbidden-phrasing verification grep (e.g. no-record-versioning-in-deliverables checks for 'previously'/'no longer'/'supersedes') is typically written as a whole-file check, not scoped to only the hunks the phase's own task list names. When rewriting one section of a long-lived doc, pre-existing occurrences of the forbidden phrasing elsewhere in the same file (describing durable system behavior, not the document's own draft history) will still fail that phase's verification unless also reworded -- even though the plan's task list never named those locations. Check the verification grep against the WHOLE file, not just the new hunk, before declaring a phase green.

git-commit-phase.sh's mechanical follow-up-commit trigger works reliably in practice: diffing .return-meta.json's proposed_file_scope array before/after a git-commit-phase.sh call reliably surfaces a silently-dropped out-of-scope path (e.g. an index-entries.json line-count sync file outside the task's declared file_scope), which a scoped git-commit-scoped.sh follow-up commit then lands cleanly without widening the pathspec or re-triggering the same drop via a second git-commit-phase.sh call.
